The scope test requires (1) a GST demand under s.73/74, and (2) the court ruling on, or being asked to rule on, a procedural complaint.

Condition (1) fails in substance: the petition challenges only a Show Cause Notice dated 11.07.2022 proposing demands under Section 74(1) (Para 2) — not a confirmed demand order. No adjudication/assessment order exists yet; the matter is still at the SCN stage.

Condition (2) also fails as actually applied: although the petitioner did raise a procedural complaint — that the SCN was issued “without considering the Petitioner’s reply” to the prior DRC-01A (Para 4) — the Court never rules on that complaint’s merits. Instead, it dismisses the petition outright as premature/not maintainable under Article 226 (Para 7–8), holding that challenging a SCN before adjudication is impermissible, and merely grants liberty to file a reply with a future personal hearing. This is a threshold maintainability dismissal, not a ruling on the procedural complaint itself.

The underlying show-cause notice is dated 05.10.2016, and the dispute concerns premiums/subscriptions under three Assam Rifles welfare schemes for periods spanning both the pre-2012 Positive List and post-2012 Negative List service tax regimes (Para 8, 12).

The demand relates to financial years 2014-15 to 2017-18 — service tax periods that predate GST entirely (GST commenced July 2017), and the dispute is between the CGST and Excise Commissioner (as appellant) and the assessee (Rishu Enterprise), on appeal from CESTAT, Kolkata.
